utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon to all. Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Just before we begin with the next witness I'd like to take a moment to introduce to the Court another member of the Prosecution team, who is seated to my right at the end, Mr. Milbert Shin. He's been working with the team for a while, but behind the scenes, and today he makes his first appearance in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Welcome, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We just wanted to confuse you further, Your Honour, with another face on our side. We're ready with the next witness, and he can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please make the affirmation which is on the card placed before you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Read it aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down now. Mr. Whiting has some questions for you. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Whiting:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please state your name.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: My name is Ramiz. My last name is Qeriqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been known by any nicknames?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I felt more honoured when I had the nickname Luani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you get this nickname?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I got this pseudonym in -- sometime in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have that pseudonym during the war in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, were you subpoenaed here by the Court to testify today?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April of 2003 were you -- did you have a summons from the Office of the Prosecutor to appear for an interview as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. On 22nd of April, and I was announced. I reported on the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell the truth during that interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I tried to tell the truth, and I believe I did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me the date of your birth, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The date of your birth again?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: 15 of April, 1962.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Kroimire is in Drenice, part of Northern Albania, which is today called Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us how far you went in your education.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Unfortunately I finished only the primary school in my native village and the high school in Lipjan. I began university studies in the faculty of biology in Pristina in 1981. But as the case was for us Albanians, the Serbs -- the Shkji, meaning the Serbs -- drove us out of the faculty, even though my faculty was not one that could create problems for them. But they did their best to drive they the authorians [as interpreted], the scholars, all Albanians from Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After 1981 when you were kicked out of the university by the Serbs, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Many Albanians, some of us were imprisoned. The intellectuals who has graduated of faculty, those who said no to the Serbs, telling them Kosova is ours, were imprisoned, whereas myself and many others were forced to leave the country. I could go to Slovenia, where my brother was working, and I took shelter there with some friends of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that were you at some point required to do your military service?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I did my military service in 1982/1983 in Slovenia. At that time it was the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: After finishing the military service, I returned to Slovenia again where my brother was to make a living, to work there, as a labourer, manual labourer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Slovenia I stayed until 1991 when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 1983 until 1991 did you have occasion to return to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, many times, many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what kind of work you did in Slovenia during that time from 1983 to 1991.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Slovenia I worked as a construction worker. Initially I worked at some firms which were Albanian and Slovenian firms, joint firms. After some time, after I learned the profession, I created my own private construction company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in Slovenia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The Slovenian people loved freedom and independence. They wanted to break away from Yugoslavia which was artificially created, something which we too, Albanians, wanted to do, but we didn't have any support. So the Slovenians began their war. At that time I became a volunteer soldier to fight on the side of the Slovenian people, to protect the children and old people. I called on my Albanian friends there. There were about 33 of us who reported there as volunteers. I informed the people concerned that we were willing and I gave them the names of the people who were willing to fight, and they told us that they would let us know if the need arose for us to fight. But the war was very brief, as you all know, and there was no need for us to join the war. We only wanted to give our humanitarian contribution to another war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to Kosovo in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. The Slovenians offered to give me their papers, nationality and so on. But at the end of 1991, in December it was, I returned to Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do in Kosovo after you returned?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I returned to Kosova and tried to do some odd jobs here and there when I managed to find a job, but most of the time I lived underground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean you lived underground?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I meant illegally from the then-government; from the Shkji, from the Serbs, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you living illegally in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Because I was an Albanian, I was born in Drenica, and my family didn't speak Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so just to be clear, who considered you to be illegal?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Who considered us? I am saying that I lived as an illegal because the Serbs at the time -- even before they had beaten me because they had the power and it was considered normal thing to beat an Albanian, and they were looking for an alleged weapon that I was supposed to have, they wanted, I don't know, to throw me in jail. They wanted to find a pretext, not only for -- in my case but in the case of many Albanians they always found a pretext just to declare them, us Albanians, as undesirable persons for the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I'm going to show you a map. It's map 6 from Prosecution Exhibit 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if it could be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, could you please find your -- the village of your birth, Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if he could be given a pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see it, sir?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I have a pen. This is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that it's -- that the witness has circled the village of Kroimire but I don't -- maybe you could use that pen, maybe it will be more clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you draw a circle --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Actually, if you could pull out a little bit for this next question on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, could you draw a circle for us, please, around the area that you referred to as Drenica. It may -- the whole area may not be on the map but that part -- whatever's Drenica on that map, could you draw a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Not the whole of Drenica is here. I can describe it in words if you want, as much as I know. Drenica is composed of several municipalities: Skenderaj; Drenoc, Gllogovc it was called before; some villages in Kline municipality; Lipjan municipality, Malisheve municipality, some villages in Mitrovica, some in Vushtrri. Maybe I have left out some villages, but these are more or less what it is comprised of. Here I see only a small part of it. This -- I see only a small part of it. Drenica is larger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I couldn't pinpoint it properly here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you've drawn a line that is in a U-shape that goes from -- approximately from Korretice, down south towards Carraleve and up around -- towards -- I'm having trouble -- Arlat and Negrovce. Is that right? Is that the line that you've drawn?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that area that is inside of that U-shape, that area is part of the Drenice region?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could this be given a number please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is P151.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, you made a reference to having been beaten by the Serb authorities. When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: That happened in 1990. I'm not accurate about the time, 1990 or 1991 probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what happened.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: It was around 11.00 in the evening. I was returning from Slovenia, where I had worked, and in a village, Rusinovce before going to my village. After Rusinovce comes Shale; then Kroimire, my village. It was there that, as I said the Serbs did with all the Albanians, they did the same to me. They asked me -- they stopped me and asked me to show the papers. He said, You didn't give me the documents properly. Put your hands on your car, they told me, and they started to beat me. But in fact that didn't weaken me; it made me stronger because I knew, and this made it clear to me, they were our enemies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many were there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you alone?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was with a relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in -- going back to the time when you returned to Kosovo in December -- at the end of December 1991, did you -- during 1992, were you involved with training people from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this training?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This training was done in our mountains, first around Kroimire. There is -- there are high mountains in a village called Karaqice. Then we organised ourselves and we -- in 1992 we reached an agreement. I was not the only one; there was a considerable group of people. And we found the best location to go and we decided to go to Tirana to get trained. It was myself, a friend of mine, Ruzhdi Saramati and Merita Mazreku. She was responsible for the girls; I was responsible for the boys. My duty was to help them cross the border.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you tell him to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, what you say has to be translated by the interpreters and you're speaking very quickly. If you can slow down a little bit so they can keep up with the translation.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I can repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think you need to repeat. Just you can continue, but just speak a little more slowly, please. You were telling us who was involved, that Ruzhdi Saramati and Merita Mazreku --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Myself and Merita were responsible to take the people to the training site. Halil Alidemaj and Ruzhdi were responsible for collecting the means and -- so that we could use them and we tried to train ourselves knowing the enemy we were facing, knowing that many times we had used the soft language, but the they didn't want the soft language so we prepared ourselves to use the language of force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and these other people you've identified, were you part of some group or movement or organisation at this time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. It was a Party of National Unity that undertook to do that. We were groups of volunteers who wanted to contribute to the national question irrespective of the sacrifices required. We were willing to lay down our lives for this purpose. People from Skenderaj, Kroimire, Prizren were involved. We had our centre in Prizren but we held many meetings in Kroimire as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bring people from Kosovo to Albania for training?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This happened -- we signed an agreement in 1992 -- we reached an agreement in 1992. In 1993 we took a group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were in the group?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Ten boys and five girls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these people from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I said earlier I think they were from the villages of Skenderaj; from my village there were some. There were some from Prizren, from the surrounding village of Malisheve. Here with me I have a photo of my friends and myself, but not of all of us were -- are in this picture. If you like, I can show it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be fine, if you could. And if you could put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This picture is ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this a picture of, please?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This is a picture of the persons who were trained for a guerrilla or frontal war to -- as the need might arise to respond to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where are you in this picture?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This person here is me. I don't think I have changed much by this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The witness has identified the person in the second row of the photograph all the way on the right, standing, with a white shirt.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here. This is me, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Jete Hasani in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. He's in the middle but he was not trained. He only helped us economically. The Serbs had beaten him, some policemen from Shtime, Godance. They had beaten him so badly he had to go to Tirana for treatment. After he recovered he met us. I knew him from before. When he saw what we were trying to do, why we were in Tirana, he began to help us financially because he got a good pay, and that's why he's there with us in the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point him out with the pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I said in the middle standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The witness has pointed to the person in a blue shirt standing in the middle of the second row.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask, with your permission, that we be allowed to make a copy of this photograph to be placed into evidence. I'm sure you want to keep the original.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: You can take it if you like. I have others at home. I can give it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: As you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I think -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If this photograph could be marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's number P152.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the training last?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Sometime between six and seven months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the training for us?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The first part of it was held in a room. There we were trained morally, physically, and psychologically. Then part of it was -- was done in the forest and then another part in the city. I will explain to you each and every one, if you want. Those who have an idea of training know what it means to get trained in the forest and in the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask a few specific questions about the training. Was there any training with weapons?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Not in Albania. Only when we returned to Kosova we did -- we used the weapons because in Albania we worked illegally, even there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me where it was in Albania that the training was actually held?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but it's a secret. It was a sports -- all kind of gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I won't press it because it's not particularly important. But did you -- you talked about bringing this group in 1993. Did you bring any other groups after that to Albania for training?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. We formed another group, but because of economic reasons we had to turn them back. And we trained them in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you do that training?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In the mountains around Kroimire, some around Pola [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you did that training, how many people were involved -- how many people were being trained?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Always in groups of ten. Sometimes in groups of five, but not more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you leading the training?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Not all of them, but I always was responsible for a group or was involved with a group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- drawing your attention to 1994, did you go somewhere in that year?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In 1994 I went to Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when in 1994?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: On the 11th of February, 1994, I arrived in Munich.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Germany?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Some friends sent me there to meet someone. There were some friends who had collected some funds for us to keep doing what we were doing. But with the friend that we started [as interpreted] we had false documents, false papers, so my friend couldn't make it. Only myself made it to Germany. And there I started to work regularly until 1998 -- excuse me. For seven months I did not report to the authorities, thinking that I would return to my homeland again but I didn't because things didn't change. So I had to report myself as a refugee and I informed them of all the problems that I had in Kosova. And they granted me asylum, gave me a German passport as a refugee, not as a German.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you worked until 1998. Can you tell us what kind of work you did.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I worked in construction and in some restaurants. After 12 we cleaned this restaurants. I worked for a firm called Whitman [phoen]. I worked for a construction company and I didn't feel shy [as interpreted] to do this kind of work because I saw there Albanian professors, academicians, doing similar jobs, even worse jobs. I remember once a professor, a former professor of Kosova University, he told me, Since you know this kind of job very well, you are a good worker, please take me as your assistant. So this is what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, did you -- while you were in Germany, did you become involved with a movement that related to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the movement or the group?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Germany I worked with several movements, but mostly with Kosova Popular Movement. There there were people of the National Unity Party and LKCK. And the PD, that is Democratic Party of Albanians. This movement was more organised; it had more activists. They were more involved in the national liberation movement and I felt -- I related better to this movement and I gave them -- I helped them. I found a hall for them to get together. I only announced the people to come to this meet -- to come to these meeting and found a place for the meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the group was called the Kosovo Popular Movement. Was that known by certain initials, that group?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, LPK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you referred to some other groups that the LPK was involved Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in, the LKCK. And what other groups besides the LKCK?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The Party of National Unity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that known by any initials?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: UNIKOMB.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other parties?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There was a party called PRSH, Revolution Party of Albanians. I mentioned those with whom -- with which I worked because there were other parties, but all of them moved towards this direction because the entire people were of the opinion that without fighting we could never be liberated. So other parties also went on the same lines. But LPK undertook to work more and to conduct the legal warfare that was organised in Kosova. And I thought that this is where I could render a greater contribution since I was trained, I felt prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to be clear, the -- and I'll ask you some questions about the LPK. The LPK advocated fighting in Kosovo to fight back against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Not only LPK, but the entire nation. They were all against the Serbs. But as I mentioned earlier, the LPK had members, had distinctive members. Many of them had been prisoned [as interpreted] and had been removed from Kosovo by Serbs by force. They wanted to leave -- to live in Kosovo, but the authorities at that time wouldn't let them so they had to leave. And to my opinion, they left the country only to return one day and not to leave it forever. That's why I think that these members had a stronger foundation as patriots and in their national work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, who was the leader of the LPK, if you know, at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I might be mistaken here. Now it's Emrush. Maybe he was then at that time. I know that these persons were there: Gafur Alushani, Ali Ahmeti, Azem Syla, and many others whom I didn't know. But mainly they were people who were well-known by the Albanians of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Emrush. What is Emrush's last name? Or family name.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Xhemajli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was located at this time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know where, but the meetings were held at the canton of Aargau in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Switzerland for meetings?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I went there when -- to ask for the permission to go and fight, not earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This was in January 1998. I had been there before, but I mainly sent messages through some friends. I went there myself in January of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go in January of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I believe that the entire world knows, not only myself, that at that time Serbs massacred many families; and simply, it was a pre-war stage in Kosova or even a war stage in Kosova. And I went there to ask them to give me a permission to come to fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you ask?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I filed a written request. The presidency was there, those persons whom I mentioned earlier, and some others whom I don't remember. And the respect I had towards them and the trust that they enjoyed, I was ready, actually, to go whenever they would tell me to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was in the written request? What did you ask for?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I asked to be allowed to come to fight, to pay for my travel expenses, because I wasn't alone. I was with several friends of mine. The time was like that. You couldn't just come to a war; you had to report somewhere. And this is what I did, I reported myself there and I came legally to join the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you asking to join the KLA to fight?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Not there but in Kosova. Maybe it was a misinterpretation because it was said to fight there. "There" was Switzerland. I was asking for permission to come and fight in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I understand that. You're right; it was a misinterpretation. But my question was: Were you asking to fight with the KLA in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Of course. The KLA was all of us who wanted to fight, all the Albanians at that time were KLA. Many times you could see the slogans on the streets "We are the KLA" because it was the only force that actually brought back the identity to the Kosova people, and I was part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you -- it was not just you, you were with several friends of yours. Do you remember how many?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: We were several, but despite the fact that I filed the request and although all of us were volunteers, half of the group decided not to come. So just one-half of the group went to Kosova. I don't know what was the reason why they didn't come. Maybe they weren't prepared enough. I think I have a paper here with me with the names of persons who were there at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The names of the persons who were with you, who went to Kosovo with you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The names of the persons who filed a request to go and fight in Kosova. And as I said, from that group there were some who went to Kosova and some who didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember who went with you to Kosovo or do you need to look at the paper that you say you have with you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Excuse me. This is the paper with the names of persons who requested to go to fight. Some of the persons who did some to fight are here on the list and some others didn't. They didn't have the means to come to Kosova. There are three or four here who actually came. Maybe there are others who joined later, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you get that list out?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I will find it now. This is the list that I comprised [as interpreted] at that time. This is the way I originally compiled it, and together with a request --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people are on that list?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There are 12 persons on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people ultimately went to Kosovo from those 12 persons?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Around six persons. Out of these 12, there are five or six. Some came after me. Maybe a total of seven, but together with me five people out of this list came to Kosova, and three or four others whose names are not on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can put that list away. When did you go -- did you get permission to go with this group? I take it you did.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I obtained the permission later in March 1998. I did have permission, but in March they called me and I went to collect the money in Switzerland, the money was with Jashar Selihu and we began our journey to Duraj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in Germany, did you know Isak Musliu?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, he was a friend of mine and we were very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he involved in the LPK?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't know. I don't know as far as this question is concerned. He was a friend of mine, a friend of my family. And we did meet during information meetings for the KLA at the time when Abedin Rexha and Ilaz Kodra were there as well and many other activists. At that time he swore an oath to join the war as well. We didn't know each other from before, although we don't live much -- far from each other in Kosovo. After he swore the oath to join the war, we were unseparable [as interpreted] in Germany, meaning I would go to see him in his apartment, he would come to my house where I was staying with my family. We would go together to these information meetings for the KLA. We went together to the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean you went together to the war?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: We came to Kosova together. The group I came with, he was there, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you went to Duraj. Was that in March of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: End of March, sometime in end of March. I'm not quite accurate about that month, but it should be late March/beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, this group that ultimately went to Kosovo, was any person in charge of the group?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The group that I came with?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of the group?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was the leader of the group or the person responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Albania, what happened?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Friends waited for us there to give us instructions how to enter Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive instructions how to enter Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the instructions?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Later on I realised that he was the general commander of the KLA. He was Azem Syla and it was a pleasure for me to meet him because to my opinion having him in such a position I thought that everything would go for the better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard of him before you went to Albania?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I had heard of him as a name. We knew him as a name, as an activist in the national issues. We respected him as a person. He was wanted by the Serbs as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: For being Albanian and for knowing that Kosova belongs to Albanians, and this is the reason why to my opinion. He knew this better than we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Albania before going into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, perhaps a week or two. I don't think it was more than two weeks. Maybe a week, ten days, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that Azem Syla gave you instructions on how to enter Kosovo. Did he tell you where to go?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He came with us up to Krume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He then gave us the instructions where to go. He gave those instructions to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he tell you where to go?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Likovc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go to Likovc?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: After some difficulties, we managed to reach Likovc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the difficulties?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Of course the border itself, it was difficult to pass the border because the Serbs had come from Serbia to guard the Albanian/Albanian [as interpreted] border. So we had to be cautious. Although it was Albanian territory, Serbs had built their border stations and were guarding the border so that we wouldn't be able to penetrate. We had difficulties. It took us several days to cross the border.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've made a few references to it, but just to be clear. Is it your view that Kosovo is part of Albania?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Historically speaking, I think it is part of Albania. And whenever I read history, it is clear to me that it has been secessed [as interpreted] unjustly and that there shouldn't -- that it isn't necessary, actually, to fight a war. But with diplomatic discussions, something should be -- a solution should be found. 90 per cent are Albanians; only 10 per cent are other nationalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get to Likovc?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: From Krume it took us almost a week to get there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you got to Likovc?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There we saw that the army was well organised and it was a pleasure for us to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet anybody?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, the person who I was told to meet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was told by Azem Syla to meet Agroni and number 10, pseudonym number 10, meaning Rexhep Selimi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bring -- give something to Rexhep Selimi?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I brought him a letter in which it was written where I was supposed to go, what were my tasks and duties, although I was told about that orally. To my knowledge in this letter it was stated that I should be positioned in Kroimire area because I came from that village and I was familiar with the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend in Likovc?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I stayed there for a week. Then I went to Klecke and then to Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Klecka, did you go by yourself or did you go with somebody?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There I accidentally met Celiku and Sadik Shala, who is a martyr now, and I went together with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went with them from Likovc to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Klecka, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you accidentally met Celiku, did you have a conversation with him? Did you talk with him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He possibly heard from Rexhep Selimi that I was going to Klecke; we didn't know each other from before. But during the conversation he asked me whether I was going to Klecke; I said yes. For me it was a great satisfaction to find out that soldiers of the KLA were in Klecka knows the geostrategic importance of this place. We didn't discuss any other matters. We just travelled together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean by the "geostrategic importance of Klecka."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Klecka was a mountainous region and it was very easy to defend ourselves from the Serbs, from the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went from Likovc to Klecka, is this still in March or is it in April?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, this was in April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the person you've referred to as "Celiku," did you know his real name?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At that time I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later learn his real name?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Later I did learn his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you learn?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I learned that his name was Fatmir Limaj, same like me when many soldiers didn't know my real name, since at that time we used pseudonyms. Someone envisioned this that it is much better to use pseudonyms than real names, and I think whoever that person was, he was right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to Sadik Shala and you said he was a martyr. Do you know what village Sadik Shala was from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: From Klecka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was he killed, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: To my knowledge he was killed during the Rahovec battle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Celiku tell you what he was doing in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, there was no need for him to tell us that because we are travelling there together. He just said that they had based themselves in Klecka, that things were doing -- going well, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- when you went to Klecka, did you stay in Klecka or did you continue right away to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I spent two nights in Klecka and then I proceeded to Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go by yourself to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I went by myself simply to organise things, to call my friends from the past and I was told -- I had the message with me to pass to them so that we all mobilise and stop the Serb forces from penetrating in villages in that area and stop them maltreating the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I stayed there two nights, then I returned to Klecka. Then I went back again. This happened for a week, Klecke-Kroimire, Klecke-Kroimire. It went on for a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this still in April of 1998 to your memory?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This all happened within a week, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that week?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I had to go back to Likovc again and take my friends who were there and together with them return to Klecke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It is U003-3680. It's been provided to the Court. It's the fourth item, number 4. And if it could be placed on the ELMO, please. If it could be raised up so the whole photograph is visible. Could it be slid up a little more, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was -- do you know when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This photograph could have been taken in the end of April or beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: On this photograph there is Kumanova, Ismet Jashari; Isak Musliu, Qerqizi; Celiku, Fatmir Limaj; and Luani, Commander Luani, who is me, myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's some handwriting underneath the typewritten text, is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This is my handwriting and I confirm now that this is what I wrote on the day when you first interviewed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just read what is written there in the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This photograph was really taken in Klecka in the oda or guestroom of Hafir Manit. The handwriting is correct, meaning I do certify that this is my handwriting. Then it's my name and signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The oda of Hafir Manit, is Hafir Manit related to Sadik Shala?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He is Sadik's father. So the oda was of Sadik, but usually we say it belongs to the person, to the head of the family, the elderly person of the family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The photograph can be taken off the ELMO. And could this be given an exhibit number, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The photograph and the translation that goes with it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Whiting, I think this might be a convenient time and we'll resume -- we'll have a break now and resume at 10 minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, I want to draw your attention to the beginning of May 1998. Were you involved in any fighting at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date of that fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At the time we were in Klecke and from Klecke we went to Lapusnik, because we could hear shots. And we went to their rescue, to the rescue of the persons who were fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else went to Lapusnik, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: We were three groups that left from Klecke. Each group had five persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there persons in charge of each group?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: One group was chaired by me, one by Topi, and one by Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody in charge of all three groups?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: It was not that there was some person in charge. In Klecke there was Fatmir, Celiku, who was in higher position, who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to the three groups that you said travelled to Lapusnik from Klecka, was anybody in charge of those three groups at that time? Just for the fighting in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: When we went to Lapusnik, Fatmir went with the first group. Then Topi and myself went with our respective groups. Topi had a radio transmitter; Fatmir didn't. We came later, maybe 20 minutes or so later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question is, Mr. Qeriqi: Was there any one person who was in charge of the three groups who travelled from Klecka to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Fatmir was in charge in Klecka, not myself, neither Topi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that he was in charge of the three groups?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, because he was responsible for the people who were in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, what happened in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Lapusnik there was a fight going on. It was a great success on the part of the KLA, but we who went there from Klecke - I'm talking about my own group - didn't do much because when we came there the war was about to finish. There was a pit [as interpreted] where -- by the Serbs was in flames. For me, this was a great pleasure to see because for the first time, I realised that we could be in a position to resist the Serb attacks, that we were capable of protecting our lands because we were in our own country. We were fighting for its liberation while all the arsenal of weapons had come there from Belgrade. I think that nature was on our side, because the means we had at our disposal compared to what the Serbs had were -- it couldn't be compared. The Serbs were more technically prepared, but the will, the just war, triumphed so we could drive them back from that place where they were stationed. I think the greatest success was scored by the other group that I didn't know, the group that was situated on the other side of the road. I think it was called Pellumbi, I am not sure. So they scored the greatest success. It -- that day the soldiers rejoiced; they were very happy. And this gave us greater strength to go on with our liberation war. We won against a greatest force. So this is how I saw that battle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, did the KLA forces suffer any losses?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't think the Serbs had any casualties but one of our soldiers was killed and another was injured. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you drove them back from that place, speaking about the Serbs. Where did you drive them back to?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The Serbs returned to their former position, to Komorane. From the position they had, they withdrew and they went back to Komorane. There is a hill called Cuka I think. Cuka, I think, in Komorane. This is where they went. Some of them settled in -- were stationed in -- at a crossroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Kris [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to another group on the other side of the road and you said you think that they were called Pellumbi. What road is that that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The road that -- the main road, Peja-Prishtine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Ymer Alushani during that fight?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him before that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I did, but not in this circumstance -- in these circumstances. I knew him as an individual, as a person. He was a person that struck everybody's eyes. He was very tall. Sometimes when I went to Komorane or some other villages, I happened to see him. So I knew him, but not in the course of the organisation fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his nickname during the war?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At that time I didn't know his pseudonym. It was an occasional meeting, but later I found out that his pseudonym was Voglushi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What village was he from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: From Komorane, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that fight on the 9th of May, do you know how long Lapusnik stayed under the control of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I think up to the first offensive. I believe so because I was not in charge of Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first offensive that you're referring to occurred when?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I think it was in July, 25th, 26th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasion of the 9th of May, how long did you stay in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Only the day of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: After that, I returned to Klecka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to -- you said that Fatmir Limaj had a unit of five persons who went. Did that unit have a name?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At that time, no, I don't know about the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn about the name later?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Later they called them "Celiku," but on the day of the fighting it didn't have a name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear the unit being called Celiku?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It might have been end of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Isak Musliu involved in the 9th of May fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit was he in? Your unit, Topi's unit, or Celiku's unit?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I want to explain. They were like squads because we were part of the same unit more or less. I don't want to be misunderstood. When we fought, when we attacked, we attacked in three groups of five. Isak was with Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- later in May did you have occasion to be involved in fighting again in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I went back on the 29th of May with three other soldiers that were -- we were four people altogether, so help there because the Serbs mounted an attack in Lapusnik. We went to a neighbourhood there, a neighbourhood of Komorane, to assist -- I said to assist. So we started to fight on the side -- on the wing. We waited until it became dark, and then the forces withdrew, went back to the place I mentioned earlier, to that crossroads, in Komorane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Lapusnik on the 29th of May, where did you come from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was in Kroimire at that time. And from Kroimire, I went to Lapusnik, that is in a neighbourhood of Komorane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: As I explained earlier, I went to assist there because we were part of the same army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. How did you know that assistance was needed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: My village and Komorane are very close. I heard the shots and I went there to help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Only that day. I arrived there in the afternoon and I stayed there until the evening and then I went back to Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During May or early June of 1998, were you involved in any other fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was involved also, I'm not sure about the date, in Ratkoc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately about the date?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember the date. I could have found out if I wanted because it is known when that battle was waged, the battle of Ratkoc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what month?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I believe it was June. I think it was June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Ratkoc?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Ratkoc is near Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Ratkoc, where did you go from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: That day I was in Klecke. From Klecke, I went to Ratkoc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Ratkoc?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: We went to help there because there was fighting going on. The day I went together with some five or six or eight persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know there was fighting going on there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I believe someone must have told us that there was fighting going on in Klecke. So a team of us left from Klecke. It was myself, Topi, and some others whose names I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, did you go on your own or did somebody tell you to go?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: We couldn't go on our own anywhere without someone telling us. When I was in Kroimire, for example, later none of the soldiers could leave the place without me knowing or without me ordering him to go to a fighting. So it was quite normal for someone to instruct us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who instructed you to go to Ratkoc?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: From Klecke every instruction came from Fatmir, as the case was with me in Kroimire or with other people in other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go back to Kroimire and focus on May of 1998 because you've told us that you were in Kroimire during that -- at times during that month. Can you tell us what you did there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Kroimire I organised the people. I -- we started work, to dig trenches, not in Kroimire but in Carraleve because Kroimire was kind of protected from Carraleve, from Zborce, Blinaje, Fushtice. So we started to dig trenches, build bunkers. We admitted new soldiers. It was the time when we came out openly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May of 1998 and to the beginning of June of 1998, how many soldiers did you have under your command in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I have a register somewhere. I think in Zborce and in Blinaje I have been less times. I had about 100 persons, maybe 70 up to 100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a soldier by the name of Ramadan Behluli under your command?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At first he was a squad commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that? When was he a squad commander?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At the beginning, in May or in June. In June I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was he based?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He was linked with us. He worked with us. He was in Carraleve. His positions were in Carraleve. He worked mostly to build the bunkers and dig trenches there. They were in the vicinity of his home, because that was his home place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever give orders to Ramadan Behluli?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know -- of course in the war if a person in a higher position assigns a task to someone, it's a kind of an order. Just to give you an example, I told him to take the positions, to build the bunkers and to be prepared, to be ready. Then when we were ready, we should attack the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told him to do those things, did you consider it -- those things to be orders?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Of course. In war this is an order. Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During -- during fighting that occurred in your area - and I'll ask you more questions about that later - but during fighting that occurred in your area, did you give orders?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I'm telling you how things happened during the war. We had a place where all the soldiers went. I, who was their commander or leader in charge of them during the war, I distributed them to several points. We didn't have so many soldier -- as many soldiers as the Serbs had. We had to spread them out by -- in threes in many places. And I consider it an order because they heard me. When I told them, Go here and there in threes, so I positioned them in these points. It's an order; it's not an agreement. We didn't have time to reach agreements. So it was a sort of order, I would say. So I ordered them to take up positions and not to allow the Serbs to enter the place. This is how it was. In the front -- they never went to the front without me being there, maybe because I had greater experience. And then also I was appointed as a kind of leader or a commander, if you like, when I was there in the war. But there is another thing. By the end of May I was not alone. There was always someone else there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you about that in a moment. But first, you mentioned that you distributed -- you had soldiers in different points. Can you tell me where those points were.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: These points were in Carraleve. I have a sketch of how we operated them. There was -- where we built our positions, but in some places we couldn't finish building the positions, we didn't have bunkers. So we had to find a suitable place to fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- excuse me. You were based in Kroimire. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you had a point in Carraleve. Did you have points in any other places around Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, in Zborce, in Fushtice, and in Blinaje. But I went less, very rarely, to the last two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about in Petrastica? Was there a point in Petrastica or no?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There was a barracks in Petrastica for the soldiers to sleep. Excuse me, but I think I understood you meaning fighting points.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You understood me correctly, and you've answered my question. You mentioned that something happened at the end of May, that you weren't alone. What happened at the end of May regarding the command of your area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I had been there earlier. I had organised the comrades. I had called on them to join, but it was not -- it was done secretly because not everybody could join, only those who we thought could join the war. I found the people who could give us food, co-villagers. At this time there was another leader who came, Shukri Buja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when he came?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I became like his assistant, his deputy. He had a greater position than me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say when he came, if anything? What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He came [as interpreted] that now I will be in charge from here to Kacanik area. But I continued to do the same job in Carraleve, to build positions and to prepare for defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Shukri Buja concentrate on particular areas? Was he more focused on particular areas?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He was more in Blinaje and in Fushtice. Sometimes he came to see what we were doing, where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you concentrated on Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who -- if you know, who appointed Shukri Buja to this position?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I cannot know this. But probably someone higher up must have appointed him. He couldn't have come on his own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that in May of 1998, Shukri Buja came and said that he was the commander of that area. At that time was there a higher command above you and Shukri Buja?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Of course there was. We weren't there without having people above us. I said from the beginning, when I came there, I came from Albania. I met with Azem Syla who was above all of us. Rexhep Selimi. I went to Klecke with Fatmir. I went to Kroimire every time. In war this is how it is. Not everybody can do what he likes. There is a chain of command. People are not appointed at will. Because if you ask the people, they might have said, You can appoint this, you should do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, at this time when was the command that was just above you and Shukri Buja? Where was it based?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I think Shukri knows better. I said I came from Likovc to Klecke, from Klecke to Kroimire. And this is how the organisation line was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The organisation went from Likovc to Klecka to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I think you must have forgotten. I said earlier that Fatmir was the commander in Klecke. In Likovc it was Rexhep Selimi. The general commander was Azem Syla. I think I already stated this earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During June and July of 1998, did you ever meet with Fatmir Limaj in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In June?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June and July did you ever meet with Fatmir Limaj in Klecka? Did you ever see him there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I have -- I met him when the fighting was going on. Otherwise at this time -- I met him but I didn't take any orders or any assignments from him because I was no longer the first person in charge, I was the second one in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met in Klecka did you tell him what was happening in your area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Not only with Fatmir, but every time we met with one other we spoke about the successes we had scored. We talked about the successes, about the work that was going on well in the front line. This is more or less what we talked about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is that answer yes, you would tell Fatmir Limaj what was happening in your area, the successes, the work --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I'm going to show you an exhibit, a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's map U003-3679. It's been provided to the parties in the court. It's the third attachment. It's 3679.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, do you see this map? Do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your signature on this map? You might have to look on the left there. I draw your attention to --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that there's a line drawn on that map? It's drawn -- do you see where the line is drawn? It's drawn around -- it's a big circle that's around Klecka. It goes from Lipovica, Carraleve, all around. Do you see that line on the map that's been drawn?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you draw that line?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that line represent?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This represents the zone -- part of the zone where I served. That is, it represents the four battalions that were in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Under Klecke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this the zone as it existed at the time that we've just been talking about, May/June 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This zone existed even before that time but my battalion was not organised in the way that I have drawn it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time -- at the time that we're talking about or even earlier, as you've said, was this zone under the command of Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: It was under the command of Klecka, but when I drew it it was as a battalion and I led that battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'd ask that this be given a number please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it can be taken off the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, to your knowledge did Shukri Buja report to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. But I would kindly ask you to see what appears on the monitor because I can't see -- it doesn't work, my monitor. Because I can see when it's being translated and I don't hurry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Shukri Buja got orders from Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This I don't know. You might ask Shukri about this. Another thing I want to say, I think earlier it was -- follow the translation if I have it on the screen. I don't want to see my picture; I want to see the text, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to put the transcript up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to fighting that occurred in your area. Do you remember when the first fighting occurred?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The first fighting which I led in Carraleve, the preparation for it, it occurred on the 14th of June. That day I felt happier than in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: That day we were prepared, we were in our positions. The Serbs started to penetrate in Carraleve and headed towards Pjetershtice first and then Kroimire. And we prevented them from advancing further. The fight was very severe, but even though the Serbs were heavily equipped and armed we managed to repel the attack. And I believe that that day the Yugoslav Army and police suffered casualties. I don't know if they died or not, but they were injured. I didn't have any casualties myself. It was the first frontal attack that we had in Carraleve. They were from Belgrade, the Serbs. Maybe there were other allies with them because I think they spoke different languages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where -- before they started to penetrate to Carraleve and head towards Petrastica, where were the Serb forces based?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: They were based in Pishat e Shtime [phoen], shtime, pine trees. Those came from somewhere in Pristina to Lipjan. They had very strong arsenal of weapons. So when they came there they attacked us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the fighting last?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: About -- the whole day I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe what -- you said they had a very strong arsenal of weapons. What kind of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know what they didn't have. They had tanks, Pragas, heavy mortar guns, machine-guns, all kinds of rocket launchers, a whole arsenal of heavy armaments up to the light weapons. That day they used all of them, they attacked all -- they fired at the village also. They used the heavy weapons against the village as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell if it was the Serb army and police or just one of the two?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Carraleve they attacked together with the army, not only with the police. I remember once it has been said not to attack the army. However, the reason why I said I felt great was because we fought with the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: We had bigger weapons than the Serb ones. One Kalashnikov that we had was much bigger than one of their tanks. We had light weaponry. The biggest one was the hand-held rocket launcher. This was the biggest weapon that we had. Then we had Kalashnikovs and sniper rifles as well as 48 rifles. There were persons who used hunting rifles as well. These are the weapons that we used and that turned to be more successful than the ones of the Serbs. They returned empty-handed. They wanted to penetrate, but their attack was repelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in command of the KLA forces in Carraleve during that fight?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was leading the battle at this time. I was a sort of commander, of course, but with a decision I became a commander later. At this time I was, as I said, a sort of commander. I led several soldiers. I accepted the soldiers who just joined. I was following the building of trenches and bunkers of the positions in one word. So I was always in the vicinity of the place where these positions were being erected. So it is quite normal that I was a person responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you direct the fighting on the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other fighting in our area after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There was on 17th of June. Until the time of the offensive there were six fights, and all of them were successful. The seventh one was not that successful. We had to withdraw from Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The seventh one, is that the offensive at the end of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the seventh fight --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The seventh, yes. The seventh fighting is the last offensive. It occurred on the 25th and 26th of July. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said there were six fights before that. Is the first of those six fights on the 14th of June and the second one on the 17th of June?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. And four other fightings, but I don't remember the dates when they occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the 17th of June, 1998. What happened in that fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: On that day, as I said earlier, I achieved a success. One of my soldiers was lightly injured. He had a scratch on his arm. So this was a successful fighting as well, and there were no damages on my side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
