utterances.text: The soldier who was injured, who was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He was Ramadan Behluli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he go somewhere to get treated for his injury?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He went somewhere, but I don't know where exactly, somewhere in the direction of Berisa. And I could have asked him where he got treated, but I didn't. It wasn't much of an injury; it was just a scratch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 17th of June, what start -- how did that fight start? What caused that fight to start? Did you attack the Serbs? Did the Serbs attack you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, we rarely attacked the Serbs. They were the ones attacking us. We mainly organised ourselves to defend from their attack and we could not attack the Serbs in our place. We were in Carraleve, which was entirely inhabited by Albanians. I don't think a Serb was ever born in Carraleve or in Kroimire in the history of mankind. If we attacked them, we would have attacked them in Belgrade or in Nis. So I don't find this question proper, whether we attacked them. It was them who attacked us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. So did you repel the attack on the 17th of June, is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasion of the -- on the 17th of June, did you see Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did he come to Kroimire, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Whenever there was fighting going on, comrades would come to assist us. Like, as I said earlier, when I went to Komorane to assist Lapusnik, they came to assist me but it was too late. The fighting had already ended. I didn't meet him at the fighting; I met him in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- during the various fights that you have talked about in your area, the six different battles, did other units ever come to help your soldiers in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Of course. There was always assistance from the person who I mentioned earlier, Ymer Alushani, and there were from all these different sides who came to assist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time when Ymer Alushani came to assist your soldiers, do you know where he came from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Of course we knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he come from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I said earlier he came from Lapusnik area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever -- let me ask you this question first: How did you communicate with other areas?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I didn't have a radio myself. Maybe someone had one, but we mainly used couriers. Then the villagers would tell us where there was fighting going on, and then we were obliged to go and assist the unit who was waging the fight. And this was a normal thing to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever send somebody, a courier, to get assistance for fighting, to get any help, for fighting in your area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I don't think I ever sent one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never? You never did --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: They came to me themselves. It is possible that I sent one, but I don't remember. Not at this time. Not at this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How -- do you know how Ymer Alushani came to assist you? How is it he knew there was fighting in your area? If you know.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: When there was fighting in Carraleve, as I mentioned earlier, Lapusnik and Kroimire were not very far from each other and firing could be heard. And when there was fighting going on in Carraleve the firing can be heard even further, even in Drenoc because they were using heavy weaponry. It happened that during a fighting in Carraleve they used mortars and rocket launchers and they killed one civilian in Kroimire, a female with the name of Afir Detaqeriqi [phoen]. How is it then possible not to hear of any fighting in Komorane or in Lapusnik when from Carraleve to Kroimire it's only 7 kilometres apart? So this is what actually made for the fighting to be heard at a greater distance. And it wasn't necessary for me to call anyone. We were under the same uniform, under the same emblem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July of 1998 did you participate in the fighting in Rahovec?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No. Although someone came to fetch me, he said that you should go to Rahovec, but we were in a state of readiness. I had only a few soldiers with me and it wasn't possible for me to go. If I wasn't in a state of readiness, I would have gone to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who came to give you that message, where did he come from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: A person came to fetch some food in Klecke and there he heard that there was fighting going on in Rahovec. And he said that whoever wanted to join the fight could go and join, but I didn't have enough soldiers. And I wasn't able to go and assist them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, do you know if somebody sent that person from Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I find this a repetitive question. I don't know if you do not understand me or maybe you forgot the answer I gave already. As I said earlier, Celiku was in Klecke and everything that came from Klecka was known that was from Celiku. The same thing was for Kroimire and myself. So everything that came from Kroimire was known that it came from me, and later on from myself and Shukri Buja. So we led that place where we were assigned to. We were in charge of the fightings, of the cause, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, do you know the date of the fighting in Rahovec in July? Do you know the specific date that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. Unfortunately, I don't know because it was a great fight, but I don't know this date by heart since I didn't take part in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the offensive that you've already talked about, you've already referred to, at the end of July 1998. Where were you when this offensive occurred?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Which offensive? You mean the first offensive?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one on the 25th and 26th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was in the fightings in Carraleve. I would again say that this was a heroic fighting. We suffered a casualty in Zborce. I lost my first soldier and it was a great loss for myself. In addition, they took up our positions in Zborce. It was impossible for us to stop them. The Serb forces on that day killed an elderly person, a civilian, paralyzed civilian who couldn't move. He was about 70, 80 years old. They played with him as they wished. They massacred him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they massacre him? Do you know how that happened?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I found out from his family that he was capped [as interpreted], tortured before he was killed. I can just reproduce here what his son told me, and he said that he was killed slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you lost your first soldier. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The first soldier that I lost was Ruzhdi Selihu, and the battalion that I led carried his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Carraleve, where did you go? You went to -- did you go to Zborce? Did you fight in Zborce yourself?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No. The fighting was going on both in Carraleve and in Zborce. They were attacking us from two different places. At that moment I was leading the fighting in Carraleve. After that, I took two soldiers and wanted to go and assist those in Zborce because they were in a more difficult position than us. But by the time I got there, the Zborce point had been taken over. In this time, an order arrived and that was for us to free the highway because the Serbs were going to attack the population. They began to shoot not only at us but at the village where the population was taking shelter, and not only taking shelter but living in their own houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This order you've referred to to free the highway, where did this order come from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This order was brought by Shukri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Shukri Buja during this fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He must have been in Blinaje and at this time he came. I didn't personally see him but the soldier told me that he told them to withdraw and that we had to free the highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Shukri Buja have a pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. His pseudonym was Kushtrimi [Realtime transcript read in error: "Kushtriti"], Gazetari, Sokoli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: It's Kushtrimi, not Kushtriti. It's written here Kushtriti and it's not Kushtriti. It's Kushtrimi with an M.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. Can you describe your -- did you have problems with Shukri Buja during this time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, we didn't have problems. It was a little bit difficult for me to accept that order for withdrawal because I was against this order for withdrawal. This was the only problem. Because it looked to me as if he did it on purpose. Maybe he didn't do it on purpose, but that's how I observed it. There wasn't any other problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean? I don't understand. What do you mean he did -- looked like he did it on purpose? Did what on purpose?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Maybe this was my opinion and could have been wrong because I didn't want to withdraw and I opposed his order to withdraw because I didn't see a reason for withdrawal. This was it, nothing more to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion about this withdrawal later on?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know if there was anything, but he justified his deed by saying that somebody else told him to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you who had told him to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At that time he said that he received an order from the General Staff, but personally I don't think he received an order from the General Staff. It isn't possible that he met someone from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after this offensive where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: After this offensive we withdrew our forces and took up our last positions. The population sheltered in the gorges while we remained in the villages in Pjetershtice, in Kroimire, and built up another defence line. We began with new positions. We began with the construction of bunkers and trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long after the offensive did you start doing this?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Immediately after the offence and maybe within two or three days. It was immediately after the offensive. It's a rule of war. When you are removed from one place, then you should build up a new defence line in another place. So it was immediately after the offensive, after two, three days, one week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the offensive, did you -- were you appointed to a position?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: For some time we couldn't see each other. I remained only with my soldier for two or three weeks, around two weeks. Later on after the offensive I was appointed a battalion commander, officially appointed according to a decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with the assistance of the usher I'm going to show you a document which is dated the 16th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: This is a document which has been supplied to Defence counsel but it has not been supplied to the Court and we have copies for the Court right now. It's also on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Of course I recognise this document. I brought you this document, and it is a document saying that from this time I am a battalion commander, and from this time I recognise the brigade as a brigade, and from this time I reported to the brigade, and from this time he was my commander; the way it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who signed this?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: With the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, did this appointment to battalion commander represent a change in the structure in your area, the commander structure I mean?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No. With the exception that Shukri was no longer there, I was alone. In other words, I was leading that battalion. Minor changes took place with some soldiers. Restructuring took place, but at this time we didn't know all the things. I was the commander, but at that time the assisting commander for logistics, for example, was not appointed and at this time now this commander is appointed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the transcript now appearing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Shukri Buja go, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: To my knowledge he went to Nerodime zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge did -- from April of 1998 until September of 1998 did Fatmir Limaj's duties change or did they essentially remain the same?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I couldn't know exactly because I did not report to Fatmir at that time, with the exception of the time when I received the decision. But it was the same person, same in Kroimire, same in Klecke. From this day when I received the appointment I reported to him. I have the material of these reportings. I held meetings with the squad commanders. I explained to them where our positions were, how many soldiers we had, how many new soldiers joined us because we had new soldiers joining us every day. So mainly I informed them about the military life in general from the 16th of August. Prior to this date, I don't know. I have nothing to say. I don't have the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, I want to take you back in time now. You testified earlier that Isak Musliu was at the fighting in Lapusnik on the 9th of May, 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he did after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know what he did after that. He remained there at that time so I don't know what he did after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He remained where?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: In Lapusnik. I know that on that day he remained in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what his position was after that time -- after that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: As I said, you asked this question earlier. I think that he could have been a platoon commander in charge of 20 soldiers, not more; but it is possible that I'm not that accurate here. Commander of a platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what time do you think that was the case? When do you think he was the commander of a platoon?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I mean before the offensive, because after the offensive Lapusnik was taken over. And this is my personal opinion and it might as well be inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After -- you said that you also participated in the fighting on the 29th of May in Lapusnik. After that, from the 29th of May until the end of July 1998, did you yourself go to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you battalion commander? How long did you hold that position?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I held the position of the battalion commander from the date on the decision up to 10th or 15th of January, 1999. So from August to January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in January 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Following the order of the General Staff, I went to Tirana in order to take some of my soldiers who had remained there injured, and to visit my family which was there at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did somebody replace you as battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I left a deputy. His name is Elez Dyrmishi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had he been your deputy?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: For some time. Earlier he was at a level of a battalion, something with logistics. But in this position he was for some two months. It is somewhere in my materials. I don't think he was in this position for more than two months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before that he had a logistics position; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you back to the time of the offensive at the end of July 1998. Did you see some people arrive on a tractor in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There were many people who arrived on tractors. I don't know -- which ones do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm speaking in particular about a group of men on a tractor shortly after the offensive at the end of July 1998. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I remember you asking me this question on the first occasion. In the beginning, I didn't remember and as the conversation went on I did. I have seen it. I know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men were on the tractor?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I believe there were 11, 12, or 13, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the men?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: They were from Godance. One of them was Shefqet and the other Adem; these were their names. My in-laws live near them and that's why I knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your in-laws live in Godance?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, they are family with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the family name of the two men you recognised?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Ramadani. To my knowledge it's Ramadani. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: They were a group of travellers. There was fighting on -- going on on that day and I was afraid that they might get killed by the Serbs. So I took them to my house. It was around breakfast time. I gave them some breakfast. And later on I assigned a person to them to show them which routes to use, routes that were without Serbs so that they could go to their house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you brought two -- brought them to your house, are you talking about the entire group or just those two men?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, just those two men. Those were the only ones that I knew. And as for the rest of the group, I also told them which route to take. But I took to my home only these two. If I took all of them, at that time it wouldn't have been possible for me to find that much space and that much food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn where these people were coming from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I didn't. But they were coming from Shale, from that area. But later on I learned -- I found them there in the morning. Early in the morning when I woke up, I found them in the village. But it's only when you told me that they were coming from that direction, otherwise I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that you had never learned where more specifically they had come from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I didn't know, no, no. I only knew where they were heading to. They wanted to go in the direction of Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if this is a convenient time, judging from when we last broke. I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it difficult to go on for another ten minutes? If it's a significant difficulty, we can break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's not a significant difficulty. We're going to head -- we're going to go into a long -- into a -- actually a long subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume at 20 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Powles had a brief matter to raise and we thought it would be convenient to do now rather than wait until the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Two weeks ago, I think on the 14th of February, the Prosecution filed the Prosecution's motion for the admission of Ramadan Behluli's prior statement as substantive evidence. As I understand it a response from the Defence is due today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: I was nominated, unbeknownst to me, to draft a joint response on behalf of the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There are descriptions for that sort of opening comment, but I refrain from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: I feel a little bit like I'm back at school not having done by homework before my teacher. It's not actually completed as yet. The Prosecution are content for the Defence to file something within a week, and my application would be for the Defence to be granted an additional seven days to draft such a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have nods on each side of me. That's a generous spirit of a new working session.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: I'm very grateful. Perhaps I could push my luck. That's in relation to the alibi notice that's also due today -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You drew that one as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: That we can have done within 24 hours, and certainly by 4.00 tomorrow it can be filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I better jump up quite quickly if I could, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What were you put in to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was put in to finalise the alibi notice and it is final as we speak, but we have missed the filing time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure you were distracted by events here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, most definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I fortunately haven't been given a task, so it's not an apology for not doing one, but it is an apology about tomorrow. May I just indicate and I hope it will be the last time I ever have to mention a trial in London; however. Last week I was due to give my final speech, however for a whole week we waited while different jurors fell ill and one fell off a motorcycle, I'm afraid, so I wasn't able to give it at all. In London they've arranged that I give it tomorrow in one day and I come back here on Wednesday. Mr. Whiting very kindly has agreed that if my learned friends go before me, which is acceptable, which is likely to be tomorrow and they don't fill out the afternoon, he very kindly will have the witness available for me first thing on Wednesday for any questions that are left. I do apologise. I'm most grateful to everyone for their cooperation. I thought I better mention it now rather than later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's fully understandable and I'm sure that it will be a great relief to you to be finally free of that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, it will. Don't let those remarks be reported in London.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh dear. And at some time before it slips the time of Mr. Guy-Smith, we have to deal with his objection to Exhibit P147.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I had thought I would wait until the conclusion of today's proceedings, but I'm more than happy to address any at this very moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think not now unless you want to say you've got nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I have a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be that if there is some time tomorrow when cross-examination has finished for those present, but before the end of our session, it may be convenient to deal with it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you have any task assigned to you, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Many, Your Honour. And the next one is to continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Splendid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Qeriqi. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, I'm going to start a different subject now and that is the subject of rules within the KLA. Did you have rules within the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to -- with the assistance of the usher I'm going to show you a document, and the ERN is U000-0445 to U000-0461.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I believe it's just -- it's being provided to the Chamber and it's been provided to Defence counsel. To be clear, this is a document that the witness brought to our attention. We had it in our possession; however, we have not translated it. We are -- we've asked for it to be translated now. I am going to, however, ask - and I've alerted Defence counsel to this - to ask the witness some questions about the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, I'm not going to ask you if you recognise this, but I'm just going to ask you if you know what this is.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I have brought this here. I have the original and you can keep this. I have mine here with me. This is a provisional rule for the organisation of the internal life in the army. I have it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, when did you get this book?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I may have obtained it in the end of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "may have." Was it before the first offensive that you obtained this book?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Before the offensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how you obtained it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I think that we had it -- myself and Shukri had this book and we had to give it to each and every soldier for them to read it. And every soldier did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember where you obtained the book from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know where it came from, but it must have come from the General Staff. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: As I said, Shukri, to my belief, brought it here and both of us had it and we gave it to the soldiers for them to read it. This happened in the end of June.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to the first page, please, and --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under the -- there's a Roman numeral I and then there's a Roman numeral II. What does the Roman numeral II say? Do you see what I'm drawing your attention to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Maybe the usher could assist in drawing his attention. I don't know if "Roman numeral" translates very well.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I know, I know. This is just an example, an example that was taken as to how to report to the 1st or to the 2nd Company. It's just an example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm -- let me draw -- you see the number 1 on that page? The -- there's 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Look at --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Oh, you mean these numbers? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You see the number 1 there? Can you read what it says there.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This is the oath and it says --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Hang on --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: -- "As a member of the KLA --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you to read a little slower so the interpreters -- and I hope the interpreters have a copy of this - they're shaking their head yes - so the interpreters could follow along. Can you read number I there. It's the oath. Go ahead and read.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: This was the oath we swore when we joined the war. "As a member of the KLA" -- excuse me. "As a member of the KLA I swear that I will fight for the liberation of the occupied territories of Albania and their unity. I will always be a disciplined fighter, vigilant and ready to sacrifice even my life for the sacred interests of the homeland. If I violate this oath I shall be punished with the most severe laws of war. If I betray, I will lose my life. I swear." This was the military oath that was taken then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were soldiers required to take this oath?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Not every day. They took the oath only once. It was just enough for the soldier to read it and he would then understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you take the oath?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Unfortunately I just read it here. On the day when it was supposed to be taken, I was on the front line and that's why I never took it, but I did earlier, during the illegal times. My oath ceremony happened even earlier, but as for this I don't remember giving it. I did swear an oath in 1992 when I went to Albania to prepare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to page 5 of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see it's 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 there.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read what's under number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "The commander is direct to their subordinates. The unit commander is the direct commander for the company soldiers."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then at the -- there's one more line I think of number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "The commander has the right to give orders to his subordinates, to check their fulfilment. It is normal for the commander to have the right to give orders to his subordinates and to check whether those orders were fulfilled."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read what -- number 4, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. On that same page, on page 5.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "The higher ranking officer has the legal right to ask from his subordinates the fulfilment of rules, regulations, orders, instructions, while the subordinate is obliged to carry out orders, decisions, instructions, and so on."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to the next page, page 6, please, and read what's under number 1, the first number 1.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "These are the rules concerning the orders and their fulfilment. The order expresses the decision of the higher ranking officer for the problem seeking solution. The orders are given in hierarchical way, orally, in writing, and with other means of communication and are obliging for -- to be carried out."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then could you read number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "Orders shall not be discussed but they should be carried out with honour, rapidly and precisely. The soldier is obliged to report to his superior for the order that he has carried out. The person responsible for the possible consequences from the order is the superior." Shall I read all of them?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that's fine. Thank you. Could you turn to page 8, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read number 8, just the first sentence of number 8.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "The soldiers are obliged to behave properly vis-a-vis the citizens and foreign journalists."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read the last sentence of number 8. That comes just --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "The persons who should communicate with them should be brief without giving any military information." I think this is normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to page 10, please. Do you see on the -- on that page there are a series of sentences that begin with the word "te" which I may be mispronouncing.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you count down to the sixth one, the sixth sentence, "te merr masa", and read that sentence.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "To take adequate measures against the persons who have violated the norms sanctioned in the rules as well as other norms that would damage the morale and the authority."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn to page 23, please. Do you see the fifth sentence down which begins "njerezve te panjohur." Could you read that sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "The military has with him secret documents. He should sleep somewhere in a family. He should leave the documentation with the commander of the closest unit and guard it."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then could you turn to page 27, please. Could you read number 1.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "In our conditions the military police is the executive civil military body that operates all over the territory of Kosova, and especially in the free territory that has been created by the Kosovo Liberation Army. It is organised and defends the military and the civilians in the territory of Kosova, supervises and regulates communication, follows up and discovers the perpetrators of military and civil criminal offences."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally could you turn to page 28. Could you read the third sentence "qu ushtarakeve".

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: What, do you mean? Yes. "That the military and the soldiers when they violate the rules shall withhold documentation, weapons, and accompany them up to the required place or given place."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The sentence after that.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "Not to use physical violence but only in those cases when they are attacked and prevented from carrying out their duties; should not use, that is, physical violence with the exception of those cases when they are attacked and obstructed from the performance of their duties."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next sentence.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "All the perpetrators of criminal offences shall descend to the respected by the end [as interpreted], together with the person, the generalities -- his generalities. Personal data." Read the other one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "Should be careful and behave in a proper way when they go into families and especially into the family that have contributed and continued to make a contribution to our national war -- national liberation war."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Shall I read it? It's good to read I think. The last one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That last sentence just before 6.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The entire 6?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. The last sentence --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Only the last one. I understood it. "It is not allowed to make use of your personal powers for personal spites or ire," I think. This is why I brought it for the Court, for the Tribunal, to see that there were rules for our army and we didn't dare do what we like or what took somebody's whim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to do a little more reading. If you can go back to page 28, there was two more that I wanted you to read on page 28.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Number 8, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "When carrying out duties in the roadblock, all the soldiers should be treated equally. The control should be made for all. With proper behaviour the traveller should be convinced that you are carrying out your duties to the people and to the homeland."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally number 10, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: "PU," meaning military police, "should always bear in mind that it carry out the activity in the war and the level of responsibility should respond to this situation. For the enemies and all those who in various forms try to prevent or sabotage our liberation war, we should be merciless. I think -- I can't read it very well. It's not a very --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just what you can read.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I can't see very well. "These rules enter into force immediately."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be given a number with the understanding that the Prosecution will provide a complete translation as soon as it's prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P156.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, you said that when you received these rules you read them and you gave them to all your soldiers to read. Did you follow -- did you follow these rules?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: That's how it was, yes. I think we followed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you require the soldiers under your command to follow them?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: We requested they did so, but there wasn't time because we were fighting. But of course every soldier had to understand this regulation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were some references in these rules to the military police. To your knowledge, when was the military police formed in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I think that in my area there were only two or four policemen for a very short time. It could be beginning of July or end of June. Sometime in end of June/beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the duties to your knowledge of the military police?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: The duties of the military police were to look after the soldiers, to check them, to check their behaviour. They helped with the civilian population. These were the tasks; for example, to see how the soldiers behaved on the streets and when there was fighting going on they came to fight with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to go into a new series of questions but before I do I would ask that the Court caution the witness under Rule 90(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, I've been asked to remind you that under the system here if you are asked a question which you think might incriminate you, you may object to answer that question on that basis. Do you understand that idea?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partly I do understand it, but if you could repeat it once again please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The essence is that you can object to -- against answering any question which you think the answer might incriminate you; that is, disclose that you yourself are guilty of some criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My coming here says that I'm ready to give answers to all the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. This is just a precaution to ensure that you are aware of your right. If you do have an objection on this basis, say so before answering the question and we can then deal with the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I swore an oath here to tell the truth and I will tell the truth for things that I know. And I don't see a need to avoid any question that has been asked -- posed to me here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if you could just keep in mind what I've said as Mr. Whiting moves on with his questions. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, do you know who Emin Emini is? Did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Emin Emini?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Is that name familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him. I know you asked me about this person during the first interview that we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when he was kidnapped on the 12th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you participate in his kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I said no. I don't even know that this person was kidnapped. I didn't hear about this. I heard when you came to interview me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear that he had been kidnapped in June of 1998? You didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. Perhaps it's the vibrancy of Mr. Whiting's tone as opposed to the question, but I believe we may be moving into that oft-complained-of area of leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it was not the substance of the question that could found any such objection at the moment, but your ears, like mine, noticed the tone. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll take, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I felt I didn't need to say that after the comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or did you Lutfi Xhemshiti?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Are you asking me? Because I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question. Did you know Lutfi Xhemshiti from Bregu i Zi?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Lutfi Xhemshiti? No, I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the Xhemshiti family from Bregu i Zi?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes. I had seen them once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to their house sometime in June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I went there for a weapon. I collected a weapon at their place and this was the first and last time for me to seize a weapon for -- from a family. I felt very bad. When I entered the house in uniform, the children were scared. I told them I -- the reason I was there was to collect a weapon; but my entering there wearing a uniform, I didn't find it just. That's why it was the first and last time I went to collect a weapon. They gave me a weapon. It was a 48 rifle. I gave it to a soldier and I never saw that family again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go -- was that -- when was that, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I couldn't be precise on the date. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what month?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: It could be June, but again I'm not precise here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it before the offensive at the end of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Before. Before the offensive I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the house, did you go during the day or did you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. go at night?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: It was night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what time at night?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the people in the house asleep when you went?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, they were awake. All of them were awake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I was with several of my soldiers. I don't remember exactly who was with me. Two or three soldiers were with me. It was evening, just before dusk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any of the soldiers who were with you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with anybody in the house?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, with one person. I don't know whether he was his brother or someone else. And to my knowledge Luta was there as well. He gave me himself the weapon and a forest ranger's uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any conversation with Luta?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No. He just gave me the rifle and the uniform. As for the uniform I said to him, I'm not here for the uniform. Thank you for the weapon. But he said, I'll give you the uniform because it's identical with the military uniform. And then I took the uniform as well, but it's not that I asked him for the uniform. His family, entire family, was there. His brother was there. I told him who I was. I gave him my name and last name, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his job was, Luta Xhemshiti's job? Do you know what he did for work?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: At that time somebody told me that he had a rifle, that he was a forest ranger and that he had a rifle. So I went there for the rifle. I didn't know anything else about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, he just said to me that, I will come, too, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say when he said, I will come?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I said to him, You'll come some other time. Today, just give me the rifle. And then he said, Okay, I will get ready and I will come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn that -- did you later -- did you learn that a few days later he was kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No. No, I never learned this. I didn't know this thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that he had been kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Later on, later on. Not at that time. Later on I just heard, did not learn about it. His wife and one of his children were there and asked if her husband was somewhere in that area. I don't know whether she was with one child or two children. It was in Kroimire. I said to her, I'm the person who came to your house and to whom you gave the rifle. And there was no need for him to be kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that happen that you spoke to his wife?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember when but she was there. It was during fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know precisely when this happened, but this was during the time that I served in the army. This was probably after the offensive, maybe September or October, but I can't give you an exact time because I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when she came to you to talk to you, what did she tell you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: She said to me, My husband is missing. Somebody took my husband. And I said to her not somebody from the army, it's not possible. Nobody from the army could take him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear anything else about what happened to this man?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a man by the name of Hetem Rexhaj coming to your headquarters in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I remember you asking me this question then and I needed quite some time to remember this person. Two brothers were serving with me and one of them was Hetem Rexhaj. Was that what you just said, that name, Hetem Rexhaj?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the name I said. Did you say two brothers were serving with you? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, two brothers. I don't know their names. They were not with us but they came to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when they came to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: One of them said, We were called to come to the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I said to him, Just one of them or both? And he said, Just one of us. And I said, Okay, one of you can stay and the other can leave. And I also said to him that I was not the person who called them and that it must have been somebody else who called them. They set off for Shale. I told my soldiers to give them directions. I had soldiers possessed in Kroimire, Shale, and Lapusnik. They headed to Shale. Now, up to which point they got I don't know. There was heavy fighting going on. It is just possible that they might have been killed in fighting by the Serbs. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "one can stay and the other can leave."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No. The one will return home while the person who has been called will stay. That person is alive. If one of them is not alive, the other is and can face me. And if these are not the words I said to him, I will be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the one who -- what happened to the one who stayed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. I just told him to proceed to Shale and that's what he did; I never saw him again. My soldiers gave him directions for Shale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I know that he went to Shale, that he set off for Shale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know anything more, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he tied up?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No. There was no need for him to be tied up. When a person comes and tells you that, I am called to join the army, then why should you tie him up?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some photographs with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: For the record the photographs are U003-2174, 2172, 2164, 2165. They don't need to be on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, could you look through these photographs, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was there put on the ELMO a moment a photograph that is subject to restriction?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The -- no, I don't believe so, Your Honour. It's a -- the larger exhibit is under seal. However the photograph itself -- I don't think there's any problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, do you recognise any of the men in those photographs?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't. I looked at all the photos, but I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything -- were you -- do you know anything about four Serb men being taken from a bus in Carraleve on the -- around the 30th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about men, Serb men, being taken -- stopped in Carraleve --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have to let me finish my question before you answer.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear anything about Serb men being taken from a bus in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a soldier by the name of Rrahman Tafa?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I knew him; now he's a martyr.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was he killed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: He was killed on the 11th of April, 1999, in Koshare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June of 1998 was he a soldier under your command?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes, Rrahman, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Ramadan Lushi? Was he a soldier under your command?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: There is not a person by this name; there has never been, Ramadan Lush.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Feradin [phoen] Gashi?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Feradin came later to be a soldier, but after the offensive, that is. Before the offensive he was there only in passing, I think, with us. He was engaged more in logistical affairs; he was not a regular conscript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you two more pictures, and for the record these are U003-8699 and U003-8700.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know him. No, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- around -- This is around the 25th of June, 1998. Did you hear anything about Zivorad Krstic or Srboljub Miladinovic being taken from a bus in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that name, the second name, mean anything to you? Miladinovic, a traffic policeman from Shtime.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember. I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Is that name familiar to you? Did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not know him. I didn't live there to know them. I told you, I lived abroad as of 1981. How could I know the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about a traffic policeman being stopped or arrested in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some more pictures. For the record these are -- it's U003-2166, U003-2167, and U003-2168. Mr. Qeriqi --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know them either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- during June or July of 1998 did you hear anything about three Serb men, two brothers and another man, being stopped and taken from their car in your area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I didn't hear and we didn't have the right to kidnap people. And I don't believe people have been kidnapped by our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you another picture. This is U003-2171.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I don't know him either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about two men being taken -- two Serb men being taken from their delivery truck in your area during June or July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear -- during June and July of 1998 did you hear of any Serb men captured in your area by KLA soldiers? Did you know of any Serb men captured in your area by KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear. I told you earlier, nobody had the right to kidnap anyone. It was not envisioned in our rules. I don't think anybody dared do that. How could I hear this when we didn't do this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some more pictures: 0323-1471, 0323-1436, U003-8705.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names Agim Ademi, Vesel Ahmeti, Shyqyri Zymeri?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I never knew them before, but after the war I heard rumours about them otherwise -- words about them. Otherwise I didn't know them. Agim that you are saying, my in-laws live in his vicinity. I know he was related to them, but I don't know more about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are the in-laws who live in Godance?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved with others in their kidnapping on the 27th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not take part in any kidnapping of these persons or anyone else. I had no reason to do that. And I don't believe anyone did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it from that answer that you have no knowledge that they were kidnapped in June of 1998. You don't know anything about that is your testimony.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ QERIQI
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that and I am certain -- I'm fully sure of what I'm saying that if I knew I would have certainly declared this before this Tribunal. But I don't know anything. My admission is that I don't know anything about this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn until 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
